commits.comment: 为 gfx950 新增 opt-in 的 MFMA 调度 LLVM-IR pass（third_party/amd/lib/Target/MFMASchedule/MFMASchedule.{h,cpp}，约 640 行）。pass 以基本块为单位切分 span（首个 MFMA 后出现的 MFMA 开启新 span，使 span 内重排依赖安全），在 span 内 hoist MFMA 输入 prep（shufflevector/insertelement）、sink 结果 extract，并用吞吐模型围绕访存锚点（GR=64 周期、LDS 按访问宽度比例）排布 MFMA，最后在每个锚点前插入 llvm.amdgcn.sched.barrier 钉住顺序；Gluon cd_regclass 的 C/D pin 随 MFMA 移动并加 fence。每块事务化调度（snapshot → schedule → verifyFunction → 失败回滚）。通过 HIPOptions.schedule_hint='mfma-schedule' 启用（parse_options 校验非法值抛 ValueError），仅在 make_llir 中 options.arch=='gfx950' 时调用，非 gfx950 接受 hint 但无效。新增 python/triton_amd.cc 的 add_mfma_schedule_pass 绑定与 TritonAMDMFMASchedule 链接库，并补充 CMakeLists、示例测试 test_schedule_hint.py（8 个用例：默认关闭/非法 hint 拒绝/交织生效/pin 保留/预置 barrier 分段/非 MFMA kernel 不动/其他 arch 忽略）。属 AMD 专属优化路径，对核心与其它后端零影响。
commits.message:
[AMD] Add an opt-in MFMA scheduler for gfx950 (#12209)

An opt-in LLVM-IR pass for gfx950 that interleaves the MFMAs of a
matrix-core hot loop with the memory operations that are independent of
them, so the matrix unit stays busy while loads and LDS accesses issue.
It is enabled per kernel through the existing `schedule_hint` option:

```python
kernel[grid](..., schedule_hint="mfma-schedule")
```

### Why

On gfx950 the stock machine schedulers leave the MFMA pipe idle for
about 30% of a GEMM hot loop: the `buffer_load`s and `ds_read`s of the
next K tile end up clustered, and the MFMAs wait on them. The LLVM pass
below spaces the MFMAs around those memory ops at the rate each op's
issue port needs, and pins the result so the machine schedulers keep it.
On the intra-wave GEMMs of the [gfx950 Gluon
tutorials](https://github.com/ROCm/gfx950-gluon-tutorials) this takes
the in-loop MFMA utilization from about 70% to 96% and TFLOPS up by
10–16% (table below). The same pass has been shipped there as an
out-of-tree LLVM plugin since the tutorials' v2.0; this PR proposes it
in-tree, where it needs no plugin loading and sees the kernel's own
`cd_regclass` pins.

### What the pass does

`third_party/amd/lib/Target/MFMASchedule/MFMASchedule.cpp`, run from
`HIPBackend.make_llir` after `optimize_module`, only for gfx950 and only
with the hint.

- **Spans.** Per basic block, the instructions are cut into spans: a
span is a run of MFMAs that ends at the first MFMA after a memory op.
The loads feeding a span's MFMAs therefore sit in an earlier span, and
reordering inside a span is dependency-safe. A block that already
carries `llvm.amdgcn.sched.barrier`s (an explicit
`gl.amd.hint.sched_barrier`, or a block-pingpong cluster boundary) is
scheduled range by range between them; nothing moves across a barrier.
- **Inside a span.** The MFMA-input prep (`shufflevector`,
`insertelement`) is hoisted to the span start and the MFMA-result
`extractelement`s are sunk past the last memory op, so the MFMA run in
between can be reordered freely. The MFMAs are then spaced around the
span's memory anchors with a throughput model: a global load gets
`ceil(64 / mfma_cycles)` MFMAs of cover (its issue path is busy for
about 64 cycles), an LDS read or write gets MFMAs at one byte of access
width per cycle with a running balance across the span's accesses, two
MFMAs drain the tail, and surplus compute is split between the span's
head and tail. The MFMA cost is the pass count × 4 cycles from
`SISchedule.td`, with the scaled f8f6f4 shapes priced by their
`cbsz`/`blgp` operands.
- **Pinning.** A `sched.barrier(0)` goes in front of each memory anchor,
so every window between fences is `anchor, mfma...` and LLVM's pre- and
post-RA schedulers keep the interleave. Machine scheduling stays enabled
everywhere else, including the prologue, the epilogue and any span the
pass skipped. MFMA accumulators pinned with Gluon's `cd_regclass` (an
empty tied inline asm on C and D) travel with their MFMA and get a fence
after the D pin; without it the machine scheduler reorders the pinned
MFMAs between anchors and leaves the pins behind as `v_accvgpr` copies.
- **Safety.** A span whose MFMA shape is not in the cycle table, or that
has no memory op to interleave with, is left alone. Every block is
scheduled transactionally: snapshot, schedule, `verifyFunction`, and
roll the block back if the IR is invalid.

### Results

MI355X, this branch on upstream `main` at 8627ec5be, the tutorial's
intra-wave GEMMs (M x N x K below, 256 workgroups), measured with the
tutorial harness: kernel time from a `rocprofv3` kernel trace, in-loop
MFMA utilization from a thread trace of the hot loop. Each cell is
TFLOPS (in-loop MFMA utilization); one run each, same GPU, stock and
scheduled back to back.

| Kernel | M x N x K | stock LLVM schedule | `mfma-schedule` | TFLOPS |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| a16w16 v9 fp16 | 4096 x 4096 x 8192 | 1415 (71.77%) | 1590 (96.15%) |
+12% |
| a16w16 v9 bf16 | 4096 x 4096 x 8192 | 1452 (71.78%) | 1651 (96.15%) |
+14% |
| a8w8 | 4096 x 4096 x 16384 | 2902 (72.12%) | 3371 (96.29%) | +16% |
| a4w4 v1 | 4096 x 4096 x 32768 | 5166 (68.02%) | 5677 (84.16%) | +10% |

commits.comment: 修复 lib/Dialect/TritonInstrument/IR/FunctionBuilder.cpp 中共享 commit-counter 辅助函数的两个 bug：(1) 计数器溢出——此前只有 AsyncCp 记录（retainCopies）才饱和到 127，其他 commit 类型（含 empty group）在多次 commit 后可回绕为负，导致合法 wait 后仍报 false race；现引入 getMaxCommitAge(commitsType)（llvm::maxIntN(位宽)）并对所有 commit kind 统一做饱和，删除 retainCopies 特判，同时将缓存函数键由 {commitsType, retainCopies} 简化为 {commitsType}；(2) wait-count 处理——大 wait count 转 i8 可变负导致 ConSan 误判为已完成、负 wait count 还会选中空 commit 表项；在 createClearOutstandingCommitsTransferCall 中对 outstandingNum 做 std::clamp(outstandingNum, 0, getMaxCommitAge(commitsType))。改动通过 llvm/Support/MathExtras.h 引入工具。该逻辑被 NVIDIA 与 AMD 共用，故新增 test/TritonGPU/consan.mlir 与 test/TritonGPU/amd/amd-consan.mlir 的 lit 用例，并在 third_party/amd 的 ConSan helper/单测中补充 async_wait_count_bounds（empty_groups/large_count/negative_count 三模式）。属 bugfix，仅影响 sanitizer 生成的检查代码，不改变 TTIR/TTGIR op 定义。

ascend_impact.functionality: 无影响。lib/Dialect/TritonInstrument/IR/FunctionBuilder.cpp 属 ConSan sanitizer 的 commit/wait 计数簿记，triton-ascend 未启用 TritonInstrument instrument pass，不经此路径；改动未涉及任何 TTIR/TTGIR op 定义（tt 方言 op/类型/属性未变），Ascend 复用的 TTIR→TritonToLinalg 转换链输入不受影响。
ascend_impact.testing: 无影响。新增/修改的 lit 与 AMD ConSan 单测仅覆盖上游 Instrument sanitizer，不影响 triton-ascend 现有测试覆盖或构建。

commits.message:
[AMD][ConSan] Fix commit-counter overflow and wait-count handling (#12208)

Fix two bugs in the shared commit-counter helpers, found while extending
gfx1250 ConSan async-copy support:

- Counter overflow: Only async-copy records retained for mbarriers
saturated at 127. Other counters could wrap negative after enough
commits, including empty groups, so later waits could not clear them.
This caused false race reports after valid waits. See representative
test:
`third_party/amd/python/test/test_gluon_cdna5_consan.py::test_async_wait_count_bounds`
with mode `"empty_groups"`.

- Wait-count handling: Large counts could become negative when converted
to the signed 8-bit counter type, causing ConSan to incorrectly consider
pending copies complete. Negative wait counts also selected empty
commit-table entries, causing ConSan to consider accesses synchronized
even though the wait did not cover them. See representative tests:
`third_party/amd/python/test/test_gluon_cdna5_consan.py::test_async_wait_count_bounds`
with modes `"large_count"` and `"negative_count"`, respectively.

Saturate ages at 127 for all commit kinds and clamp ConSan's wait
thresholds to [0, 127]. These fixes apply to the common bookkeeping used
by AMD and NVIDIA.

commits.message:
[triton_kernels] Support four-column Blackwell activation scale alignment (#12213)

Allow Blackwell activation scales to use four-column padding when
eight-column padding would waste storage. Callers can opt in with
`BlackwellActMXScaleLayout(None, column_alignment=4)`; the default
remains 8 and the 128×4 swizzle is unchanged. Reject alignments other
than 4 or 8, and repack storage when converting between the two
alignments.

Add CPU regression tests for the compact layout's storage shape and
round trip, plus conversion from 4 to 8 and back. The two new tests and
nearby storage-shape, symbolic-shape, ragged-shape, and no-op conversion
tests pass: 37 cases, using the local `triton_kernels` code with the
installed Triton package. No GPU tests were run.

commits.message:
Tune Gluon FA example for Rubin (#12200)

Following [the existing style of kernel-knobs
tuning](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/main/python/examples/gluon/01-attention-forward.py#L1039-L1088),
I did a sweep for Rubin. This forms the baseline for Rubin attention
optimizations.

Also fixed unrelated issues:
* The combination of `causal = True` and `use_tmem_red = True` has been
buggy. TMEM load reduction computes row max over unmasked scores, but
row max needs to be computed on masked score. So the correct
implementation skips using TMEM load reduction for diagonal blocks. cc
@3gx
* `select_kernel_config` function does not honor the value of
`use_tmem_red` from the benchmark driver. When we run
`01-attention-forward.py`, we want to see the speedup from `use_tmem_red
= True`. But since `select_kernel_config` may select `use_tmem_red =
True` even if the benchmark driver wants to evaluate `use_tmem_red =
False`, for example, the benchmark results look like the choice of
`use_tmem_red = True / False` has no effect. Fixed by introducing a
wrapper `select_benchmark_kernel_config` which always selects the value
of `use_tmem_red` as requested by the benchmark driver.
